author: Bobby Grayson

metadata.prompt:
REJECTED: Strict delete (require edges removed first)

Why this was rejected:
- User is already frustrated by inability to fix mistakes
- Adding MORE steps (delete each edge individually) compounds frustration
- Error message "cannot delete node with edges" doesn't help user
- Would require users to run: deciduous edges | grep <node_id> 
  then delete each edge one by one before deleting the node
- Against the goal of making mistake correction easy

When strict might make sense (but not here):
- Multi-user systems where cascade could break others' work
- Audit requirements where every deletion must be explicit
- Complex systems where cascade side effects are non-obvious

For deciduous (single-user local tool), cascade is clearly better UX.

title: Strict delete: require all edges removed before node deletion
